title: Pleasant to people (Avot 3:10)
hook: whoever is pleasing to people is pleasing to God
tomorrow: where does a whole day go?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Chanina ben Dosa's rule: deeds first, so the wisdom lasts. He has one more saying, and it's about how other people feel when you walk in.

Opening night, five o'clock, and somebody's already snapped at the kid running the lights. Can being liked by people mean anything to God? Chanina ben Dosa says it does. In Avot: whoever the spirit of people is at ease with, the spirit of God is at ease with. And whoever the spirit of people isn't at ease with, neither is the spirit of God. The way people breathe around you, he says, is a clue to how heaven does.
screen: `FIVE O'CLOCK, OPENING NIGHT.` → `PEOPLE AT EASE WITH YOU.` → `GOD AT EASE WITH YOU.`

segments.voice: Start with the word he uses for people: briyot, creatures. Not one group, not the people who agree with you; everyone God made. Hillel uses the same word back in chapter one, loving the creatures. So the measure is wide. The lighting kid counts. The stranger at the counter counts. Second, the word for pleased is nochah, at ease, settled. It isn't about being popular, or agreeing with everyone so nobody's ever upset. It's whether people can rest around you: whether your presence makes a room easier or harder to breathe in. Third, the life version. A hard week, a short temper, an apology that's late but real. Being pleasant to people is a practice, not a personality; it's built one interaction at a time, often right after you've blown one. Fourth, the hard edge. It's a demanding test, because it's checked by the people around you, not by your own opinion of yourself. Chanina ben Dosa puts God's ease and people's ease side by side, so how someone treats the creatures can't be separated from how they stand with the Creator.
screen: `BRIYOT: EVERYONE GOD MADE.` · `AT EASE, NOT POPULAR.` · `A PRACTICE, NOT A PERSONALITY.` · `CHECKED BY THE PEOPLE AROUND YOU.` · then, large: `PLEASANT TO PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Let your face soften, jaw, forehead, the skin around your eyes, the way it does when someone you're glad to see walks in. Hold that ease through a few slow breaths. Then bring to mind one person you've been short with lately, and keep the softness while you think of them.
Pleasant to people: when the spirit of people is at ease with someone, Chanina ben Dosa says, so is the spirit of God.
Your line: pleasant to people. Everyone counts, starting with whoever happens to be nearest. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish ethical teaching, from Avot to the Mussar tradition, treats pleasant, respectful dealing with every person as part of serving God, not separate from it.
